Retail and e-commerce translation services

October 15, 2021
Retail | E-commerce

If you want your online store to serve customers abroad, translation is one of the first things to get right. A shopper who cannot understand your product page, delivery terms or returns policy will not buy from you, however good your range is.

Retail translation is not the same as general translation. It combines marketing copy, technical product details and legal information, and each part needs a different skill.

What retail translation covers

Online retail has its own rules. Your customers cannot touch the product or speak to a sales assistant, so your text has to do that work for them.

That text includes more than product descriptions:

  • product titles, descriptions, specifications and size guides
  • category pages, menus and search filters
  • basket, checkout and payment messages
  • delivery, returns and refund policies
  • customer reviews, emails and customer service templates
  • packaging, labels and instructions for use
  • campaigns, promotions and social media content

Consumer goods translation adds packaging and instructions to this list, where accuracy matters as much as appeal.

Why a literal translation fails in an online store

Customers decide quickly. A product name that sounds odd, a size chart in the wrong units or a checkout message that reads like a machine wrote it all create doubt at the point of purchase.

A good retail translator adapts your content to the local market. They adjust tone, units, currency, date formats and sizing, and they choose the words local shoppers actually search for. Colours, images and slogans can also carry different associations in different cultures, so a local review is worth building into your process.

This is why website translation and localisation from a specialist works better than a word-for-word conversion. The aim is a store that feels as though it was built for your customer, so they probably will not realise they are using a translated page.

Legal and safety information when you sell into Europe

Some of your retail content is a legal obligation as well as a sales tool. In France, the Toubon law requires French to be used in the description, offer and presentation of a product, in instructions for use, in the description of warranty terms and on invoices. The consumer protection authority, the DGCCRF, enforces it.

The EU General Product Safety Regulation asks for clear instructions and safety information in a language consumers can easily understand. As a UK business selling to EU consumers, you sit outside the EU, so check with a legal adviser what the regulation requires of you before you list products.

A translator cannot give legal advice, but a specialist can make sure the wording you need is accurate in every language you sell in.

Translation for the markets you sell in

Each market has its own expectations. We provide French e-commerce, German e-commerce and Korean consumer and retail translation, plus Spanish retail and e-commerce translation.

If you are unsure where to start, tell us which countries you ship to and which products sell best. We can advise on which pages to translate first, and a translator who specialises in retail will keep your brand voice consistent across them.

The advantages of good retail translation

  • Your site feels as relevant in each language as the one you built in English.
  • Your brand voice and key terms stay consistent across pages, emails and packaging.
  • Product names, slogans and terminology fit the local market and avoid awkward or unintended meanings.
  • Your international customers have a smooth, user-friendly experience that helps them buy with confidence.

Interpreting for retail buyers and suppliers

Retail also runs on conversations with suppliers, buyers and distributors. If you need to negotiate or run a meeting in another language, remote interpreting lets you work with an interpreter without the cost of travel.

How do you know your retail translation is working?

Once your translated store is live, check that it is doing its job. A few signals tell you quickly:

  • Sales, conversion and basket abandonment in each target market compared with your home site.
  • Questions and complaints to customer service about unclear wording.
  • Return reasons that point to misunderstood descriptions or sizes.
  • Product names, slogans and search terms that read naturally to a native speaker.
  • A full test of the checkout in each language.

If sales do not take off in a target country, your site may not have been translated thoroughly. Perhaps product names that should have changed did not, or descriptions read like a literal conversion of the source text.

If your translated site is working, your linguist has most likely respected your requirements and produced an adapted text instead.

Start your retail translation project

If you need a reliable professional translation service for your online store or product range, our team at BeTranslated can help. We quote per project, so you receive a clear price for the pages, languages and formats you need.

To discuss your project, email hello@betranslated.co.uk or call +442030269848. You can also send your files through our quote request page for a free, no-obligation quote.

Frequently asked questions

What is retail translation?

Retail translation adapts the content your shoppers read, such as product pages, checkout messages, policies and packaging, into another language. It goes beyond words to cover tone, units, sizes and local expectations.

Do you translate online store content?

Yes. We translate product catalogues, category pages, checkout flows, emails and policies for e-commerce sites. Send us your content files and we will confirm the best way to handle them.

Which languages do you cover for e-commerce?

We cover French, German, Spanish, Korean and many other languages for retail and e-commerce. Tell us your target markets and we will confirm availability.

Do I have to translate product information by law?

It depends on where you sell. France, for example, requires French in the presentation and instructions for products sold there, and EU rules on product safety ask for information consumers can understand. Check your obligations for each market with a legal adviser.

How much does retail translation cost?

The cost depends on the number of words, the languages, the amount of specialist content and your deadline. We quote per project, so send your content and you will receive a clear quote.
